result.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
result.summary: Continual learning in physical AI differs from conventional continual learning because small per-step policy errors can accumulate over a trajectory. Each deviation may move the agent outside the training distribution, increase subsequent prediction errors, and ultimately cause closed-loop task failure. This work introduces Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity (DRAP), a replay-free method that estimates the historical importance of adaptable model tensors from sample-level action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk. A ridge-regularized local linear model is fitted to expert state-action transitions, and the largest singular value of its state-transition matrix provides a policy-independent, Lyapunov-inspired estimate of one-step perturbation amplification. After each task, risk-weighted squared gradients are accumulated in a tensor-level importance memory. During subsequent tasks, DRAP uses normalized cumulative importance to scale the effective AdamW learning rate of each tensor, immediately reducing the plasticity of components that supported previous behavior at dynamically sensitive trajectory points. We instantiate DRAP on a fixed KappaTune-selected subnetwork of OpenVLA and evaluate replay-free sequential adaptation across the LIBERO Spatial, Object, and Goal suites. Compared with standard AdamW fine-tuning and EWC, the results show substantially improved retention of previously learned behaviors while preserving strong new-suite acquisition.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DRAP，一种无回放的持续学习方法：用专家状态-动作转移拟合局部线性模型，以状态转移矩阵最大奇异值作为单步扰动放大风险的估计，按风险加权动作梯度累积张量级重要性，并据此缩放后续任务中各张量的 AdamW 有效学习率；在 OpenVLA 子网络上评测 LIBERO 顺序适配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按轨迹局部动力学敏感度加权梯度重要性、再调节张量可塑性」的机制，可能为 latent 多步推理中的状态漂移控制与参数保护、贡献分配提供借鉴线索；但研究对象是机器人动作策略而非推理状态，需核查是否可迁移。
